name: FC Astana
content:
FC Astana is a professional football club based in the capital city of Astana, Kazakhstan. Founded in 2009 as Lokomotiv Astana, the club was rebranded to its current name in 2011. It competes in the top tier of Kazakh football, the Kazakhstan Premier League, and plays its home matches at the Astana Arena, a modern stadium with a capacity of over 30,000 spectators.

Despite its relatively short history, Astana has quickly become the most dominant club in Kazakhstan. The team has won multiple league titles, as well as several domestic cups and super cups, establishing itself as a powerhouse in national football. Their consistent success has been driven by strong financial backing and effective management, allowing them to attract quality players and coaches.

Astana has also made a significant impact in European competitions, becoming the first Kazakh club to reach the group stage of the UEFA Champions League in 2015. This achievement marked an important milestone for football in Kazakhstan and raised the club’s international profile. Since then, Astana has regularly participated in European tournaments, contributing to the growing reputation of Kazakh football on the continental stage.

name: FC Kairat
content:
FC Kairat is a professional football club based in Almaty, Kazakhstan, and one of the most historic and widely supported teams in the country. Founded in 1954 as Lokomotiv Alma-Ata, the club was renamed Urozhay in 1955 and adopted the name Kairat in 1956. It currently competes in the Kazakhstan Premier League and plays its home matches at the Central Stadium.

During the Soviet era, Kairat was the leading club from Kazakhstan and the only representative of the Kazakh SSR in the Soviet Top League, where it spent many seasons competing against top teams from across the USSR. Because of this role, the club earned the nickname “The Nation’s Team” and built a strong fan base across the country. It also achieved success in the Soviet First League, winning the title twice and maintaining a consistent presence in high-level competition.

In the post-independence period, Kairat has remained one of the most successful clubs in Kazakhstan, winning multiple league titles, national cups, and super cups. The team has developed a strong rivalry with FC Astana, with their matches often referred to as the “Two Capitals Derby.” In recent years, Kairat has also been a regular participant in European competitions, contributing to the growing international profile of Kazakh football.

name: FC Irtysh
content:
FC Irtysh Pavlodar is a professional football club based in the city of Pavlodar, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1965, it has played its home matches at the Central Stadium and has long been one of the most prominent teams in Kazakh football. The club was among the founding members of the national top division after independence and spent many years competing at the highest level of the country’s football system.

Irtysh Pavlodar is considered one of the most successful clubs in Kazakhstan, particularly in the early post-Soviet era. The team won the Kazakhstan Premier League five times (1993, 1997, 1999, 2002, and 2003) and also claimed the Kazakhstan Cup in 1998. Internationally, the club participated in Asian competitions before Kazakhstan joined UEFA, reaching the semi-finals of the Asian Club Championship in 2001, and later appeared in European tournaments such as the UEFA Champions League qualifiers.

Throughout its history, the club underwent several name changes, including Traktor, Ansat, and Irtysh-Bastau, before returning to the name Irtysh. Despite its strong legacy, the club faced serious financial difficulties and withdrew from the top division in 2020, effectively ceasing operations for a period. It was later reformed and re-entered the lower leagues, beginning a gradual return to professional football in Kazakhstan.

name: FC Aktobe
content:
FC Aktobe is a professional football club based in the city of Aktobe, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1967 as Aktyubinets, the club has undergone several name changes, including Aktobemunai, Aktobe, and Aktobe-Lento, before returning to its current name in 2005. It competes in the top tier of Kazakh football, the Kazakhstan Premier League, and plays its home matches at the Central Stadium, which holds around 13,000 spectators.

Aktobe is one of the most successful clubs in Kazakhstan, particularly during the 2000s. The team has won five league titles, along with multiple domestic trophies including the Kazakhstan Cup and Super Cup. Its most dominant period came between 2005 and 2009, when it established itself as a leading force in national football. The club also achieved success during the Soviet era, winning the Soviet Second League twice.

In addition to domestic success, Aktobe has regularly participated in European competitions such as the UEFA Champions League and Europa League qualifiers. The club is known for its strong fan base and consistent performances at home, where it has set notable unbeaten records. Despite fluctuations in results over the years, FC Aktobe remains one of the most recognized and historically significant teams in Kazakh football.

name: FC Yelimay
content:
FC Yelimay is a professional football club based in Semey, Kazakhstan, with a long and complex history dating back to 1964. The team plays its home matches at the Spartak Stadium and currently competes in the Kazakhstan Premier League. Although officially re-established in 2022, the club is widely regarded as the continuation of earlier teams from Semey, including Spartak and Yelimay, maintaining a strong historical identity in Kazakh football.

The club was particularly successful in the early years following Kazakhstan’s independence, when it competed under the name Yelimay Semey. During the 1990s, it became one of the dominant forces in the national league, winning three Kazakhstan Premier League titles in 1994, 1995, and 1998, as well as the Kazakhstan Cup in 1995. Its success during this period established it as one of the leading clubs in the country’s football history.

Over time, the club underwent numerous name changes, including Tsementnik, Spartak, AES-Yelimay, and Semey, reflecting shifts in sponsorship and organization. After financial difficulties led to its dissolution in 2016, the club was revived in 2022 under the Yelimay name and quickly returned to prominence by winning the Kazakhstan First Division in 2023 and earning promotion back to the top tier. Today, FC Yelimay continues to rebuild its legacy while competing at the highest level of Kazakh football.

name: FC Zhenis
content:
FC Zhenis is a professional football club based in Astana, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1964, it is one of the historic teams in Kazakh football and a founding member of the national top division after independence. The club plays its home matches at the Kazhymukan Munaitpasov Stadium and currently competes in the Kazakhstan Premier League.

Throughout its history, the club has undergone numerous name changes reflecting political and organizational shifts, including Dinamo, Tselinnik, Tsesna, Astana, and Astana-1964 before returning to the name Zhenis. It enjoyed its most successful period in the early 2000s, winning three Kazakhstan Premier League titles (2000, 2001, and 2006) as well as several Kazakhstan Cup trophies.

Despite its success, the club faced financial difficulties and was declared bankrupt in 2009, leading to relegation from the top division. In the following years, it struggled in lower leagues and even temporarily ceased operations before being revived by supporters. After its reestablishment, FC Zhenis gradually returned to professional football and has since regained a place in the top tier, continuing to rebuild its legacy in Kazakh football.

name: FC Tobol
content:
FC Tobol is a professional football club based in Kostanay, Kazakhstan, founded in 1967. The team plays its home matches at the Central Stadium and has been a постоян participant in the Kazakhstan Premier League since the league’s creation in 1992. Over the decades, the club has built a reputation as one of the most stable and competitive sides in Kazakh football.

Throughout its history, the club has undergone several name changes, including Avtomobilist, Energetik, Kustanayets, and Khimik, before adopting the name Tobol in 1995. Its most successful period began in the early 2000s, when the team consistently finished near the top of the league standings. Tobol achieved major domestic success by winning the Kazakhstan Premier League in 2010 and again in 2021, along with multiple national cup and super cup titles.

The club has also made its mark in international competitions. Tobol won the UEFA Intertoto Cup in 2007, becoming one of the few Kazakh teams to claim a European trophy. In addition, the team has regularly participated in UEFA competitions, helping to raise the profile of Kazakh football abroad. Today, FC Tobol remains a strong and competitive club, continuing to challenge for domestic honors and represent Kazakhstan in European tournaments.

name: FC Shakhter Karagandy
content:
FC Shakhter Karagandy is a professional football club based in the city of Karaganda, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1958, it is one of the oldest clubs in the country and plays its home matches at the Shakhter Stadium. The team has been a regular participant in the top tier of Kazakh football since the formation of the national league in 1992, although it was relegated to the First Division after the 2024 season.

The club achieved its greatest success in the early 2010s, when it won back-to-back Kazakhstan Premier League titles in 2011 and 2012. It also secured the Kazakhstan Cup and Super Cup in 2013, marking the most successful period in its history. Known as “The Miners,” Shakhter built a reputation as a strong and disciplined team, capable of competing consistently at the top level of domestic football.

Shakhter Karagandy has also made notable appearances in European competitions, representing Kazakhstan in tournaments such as the UEFA Champions League and Europa League qualifiers. One of its most significant achievements came in 2013, when it reached the play-off round of the Champions League and later competed in the group stage of the Europa League, becoming one of the first Kazakh clubs to reach that level.

name: FC Taraz
content:
FC Taraz is a professional football club based in the city of Taraz, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1960, the club is one of the older football institutions in the country and has participated in Kazakh and Soviet competitions under several different names throughout its history. It plays its home matches at the Central Stadium in Taraz and has long been considered an important representative of southern Kazakh football.

The club has undergone multiple name changes reflecting different eras and sponsorship periods. It was originally established as Metallist and later known as Voskhod, Energetik, Alatau, Khimik, and Fosfor before finally adopting the name Taraz in 1994. These changes were typical for many post-Soviet clubs, especially during periods of economic and structural transition in the 1990s.

Taraz achieved its greatest success in the mid-1990s, when it became one of the strongest teams in Kazakhstan. The club won the Kazakhstan Premier League title in 1996 and lifted the Kazakhstan Cup in 2004, marking its main domestic achievements. Although it has experienced ups and downs since then, including relegations and returns to the top flight, FC Taraz remains a recognizable and historically significant club in Kazakh football.

name: FC Ordabasy
content:
FC Ordabasy is a professional football club based in Shymkent, Kazakhstan, competing in the Kazakhstan Premier League. The club traces its origins back to 1949, although its modern identity was formed through the merger and reorganization of earlier local teams, most notably FC Zhiger and FC Tomiris, which were combined into a single structure in the early 2000s. Over time, the club adopted the name Ordabasy and established itself as the main representative of football in southern Kazakhstan.

Historically, the club’s development reflects the broader restructuring of Kazakh football after independence. It went through several transformations, including periods of financial instability and rebranding, before stabilizing under the Ordabasy name. The team gradually built a reputation as a competitive mid-table side in the domestic league, known for its solid organization and ability to challenge stronger opponents in key matches.

In recent years, FC Ordabasy has become more successful on the national stage, regularly competing for top positions in the league and achieving success in domestic cup competitions. The club has also participated in European tournaments, representing Kazakhstan in UEFA qualifying rounds. With improving performances and growing consistency, Ordabasy has established itself as one of the more stable and ambitious clubs in Kazakh football.

name: FC Kyzylzhar
content:
FC Kyzylzhar is a professional football club based in Petropavl, Kazakhstan, competing in the Kazakhstan Premier League. The club was founded in 1968 and has long been considered one of the traditional teams in northern Kazakhstan. It plays its home matches at Karasai Stadium and has been a regular participant in the country’s top division since independence, with occasional relegations and returns over the years.

Throughout its history, the club has gone through numerous name changes, reflecting different eras and organizational shifts. It started as Avangard and later became Metallist, before continuing under names such as Esil, Access-Esil, Esil-Bogatyr, and eventually adopting the name Kyzylzhar in 2009. These transformations were typical for post-Soviet football clubs, especially during periods of financial and structural instability.

Kyzylzhar’s strongest period came in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when it achieved its best league results, finishing as runner-up in 1999 and 2000. In more recent years, the club has generally operated as a mid-table side but has remained stable in the Premier League. It continues to focus on developing competitiveness and maintaining its place among Kazakhstan’s established football clubs.

name: FC Atyrau
content:
FC Atyrau is a professional football club based in the city of Atyrau, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1980, the club competes in the Kazakhstan Premier League and plays its home matches at the Munaishy Stadium. The team is nicknamed “The Oilers” due to the region’s strong connection with the oil industry, which is also reflected in the club’s identity and symbolism.

The club’s origins date back to the Soviet period, when it was originally established under the name Prikaspiets. It played in lower Soviet leagues before being reformed after Kazakhstan’s independence. In 2000, the club was revived as Akzhaiyk and soon after adopted the name Atyrau when it earned promotion to the top division. Since then, it has become a stable presence in Kazakh top-flight football.

FC Atyrau has had a modest but notable history in domestic competitions. Its most significant achievement is winning the Kazakhstan Cup in 2009, and it has also reached the final on other occasions. While not among the most decorated clubs in the country, Atyrau is known for its competitiveness and ability to challenge stronger teams, as well as for maintaining a consistent place in the national football system over the years.

name: FC Ekibastuzets
content:
FC Ekibastuzets is a professional football club based in Ekibastuz, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1979, the club has spent most of its history competing in the country’s top and second tiers. It plays its home matches at Shakhtyor Stadium and was among the early participants in the Kazakhstan Premier League after the country gained independence.

The club has gone through several name changes throughout its history, reflecting different eras and organizational shifts. It began as Ugolshik, later became Ekibastuzets, and was also known as Batyr and Ekibastuzets-NK before returning to its established name. These changes were common for many Kazakh clubs during the post-Soviet transition period.

Ekibastuzets experienced its most notable results in the 1990s and early 2000s, when it finished as runner-up in the national league on multiple occasions and remained competitive in the top division. However, the club also faced instability, including relegations and eventual withdrawal from the Premier League in the late 2000s. Since then, it has continued to exist in lower divisions, maintaining its role as a traditional football team from Ekibastuz.

name: FC Zhetysu
content:
FC Zhetysu is a professional football club based in Taldykorgan, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1981, the club has been a regular participant in Kazakh football and is considered one of the traditional teams in the country. It plays its home matches at Zhetysu Stadium and has spent most of its history competing in the Kazakhstan Premier League, with occasional relegations and promotions between divisions.

Throughout its history, the club has gone through several name changes reflecting different periods and sponsors. It was originally founded as Zhetysu, later renamed Taldykorgan in 1993, Kainar in 1994, and Zhetysu Promservice in the late 1990s before returning to the name Zhetysu in 1999. These changes were typical for Kazakh clubs during the post-Soviet transition, when financial instability often influenced club identities.

Zhetysu has not won the national league title but has achieved respectable results over the years, including finishing in the upper part of the table in several seasons. The club has also participated in domestic cup competitions and occasionally qualified for European tournaments, though without major success. Overall, FC Zhetysu is seen as a stable mid-level club with a long-standing presence in Kazakh football.

name: FC Gornyak
content:
FC Gornyak is a defunct Kazakh football club based in Khromtau, founded in 1990. The team mainly competed in the early years of Kazakhstan’s football system after independence, participating in national league competitions. It played a role in the development of regional football during the transition period of Kazakh sports in the 1990s.

During its existence, Gornyak had fluctuating performances in domestic competitions. The club even started a Premier League season in 1996 but withdrew early, with its results being annulled. Financial and organizational difficulties repeatedly affected its stability, which limited its ability to remain consistently in the top tier of Kazakh football.

In the 2000s, the club continued to struggle in lower divisions and eventually faced ongoing financial problems. These issues led to its withdrawal from competition during the 2008 season, after which the club effectively ceased operations. Despite its dissolution, FC Gornyak is remembered as part of the early history of professional football in independent Kazakhstan.

name: FC Zhiger
content:
FC Zhiger was a football club based in Shymkent, Kazakhstan. It was originally established in 1960 as Metallurg, and over the years the club went through several name changes before becoming Zhiger in 1992. The team represented one of the key football traditions in southern Kazakhstan and competed in the early seasons of the country’s top football competitions after independence.

In the 1990s, Zhiger played an important role in Kazakh football, participating in the national league and serving as one of the main clubs from Shymkent. However, like many post-Soviet teams, it faced financial instability and organizational difficulties. These issues affected its consistency and long-term competitiveness at the highest level.

In 2000, FC Zhiger was dissolved as part of a merger with FC Tomiris, which led to the creation of a new club, FC Dostyk. This merger marked the end of Zhiger as an independent team, but its legacy continued indirectly through successor clubs, which later evolved into FC Ordabasy.

name: FC Kaisar
content:
FC Kaisar is a professional football club based in Kyzylorda, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1968, it is one of the country’s older football teams and has been a regular participant in Kazakh football since the Soviet era. The club plays its home matches at the Gani Muratbayev Stadium and is considered an important representative of football in the Kyzylorda region.

Throughout its history, FC Kaisar has undergone several name changes, including Volna, Avtomobilist, Orbita, Meliorator, and Kaisar-Munai, before finally stabilizing under the name Kaisar in the early 2000s. It was one of the founding members of the Kazakhstan Premier League after independence and has spent most of its existence moving between the top division and the second tier.

The club’s most successful period came in 1998 and 2019, when it won the Kazakhstan Cup twice, which remains its main achievement in domestic football. Kaisar is known for its resilience and ability to return to the top flight after relegations, often relying on local talent and limited resources compared to the country’s biggest clubs.

name: FC Vostok
content:
FC Vostok was a professional football club based in Oskemen, Kazakhstan. Founded in 1963, it was one of the early established football teams in the country and later became a founding member of the Kazakhstan Premier League after independence. The club played its home matches at Vostok Stadium and represented the eastern region of Kazakhstan throughout most of its existence.

During its history, Vostok experienced mixed sporting results, with its strongest league performances coming in the late 1990s when it finished 5th in consecutive seasons. The club also achieved domestic success by winning the Kazakhstan Cup in 1994, which remains its main trophy. Despite these highlights, Vostok often struggled with consistency and stability in the top division.

In the 2000s and 2010s, the club faced serious difficulties, including financial problems and disciplinary issues that affected its long-term survival. It was eventually expelled from the Kazakhstan Premier League and ceased operations in 2016. After its dissolution, the club’s structure and football presence in the region were effectively absorbed into later reorganizations of local teams in Oskemen.

name: FC Alma-Ata
content:
FC Alma-Ata was a professional football club based in Almaty, Kazakhstan. It was founded in 2000 under the name FC Tsesna and later rebranded as Alma-Ata in 2004 after achieving promotion to the Kazakhstan Premier League. The club played its home matches at the Central Stadium in Almaty and competed in the top division during the mid-2000s.

The team’s most successful period came in 2006, when it achieved its highest league finish and won the Kazakhstan Cup, which marked its only major trophy. This victory also earned the club qualification for European competition, where it participated in the UEFA Cup qualifiers. Despite this success, the club struggled to maintain stability in subsequent seasons.

In 2008, FC Alma-Ata faced severe financial difficulties, which led to bankruptcy and its eventual dissolution. After the club ceased operations, many of its players and staff moved to other teams, and its place in Kazakh football history is mainly remembered for its short but eventful existence and cup-winning achievement.

name: FC Dostyk
content:
FK Dostyk Almaty was a football club based in Almaty, Kazakhstan. It was founded in 1990 and quickly became part of the early structure of Kazakh football during the transition period following the collapse of the Soviet Union. The club competed in the newly formed national competitions and represented one of the short-lived teams from the early independence era.

In 1993, Dostyk was admitted to the Kazakhstan Super League, where it had a surprisingly strong debut season. The team performed well in the early stage of the competition and achieved one of its greatest successes by winning the Kazakhstan Cup in the same year, defeating FC Taraz in the final. Despite this achievement, the club did not manage to establish long-term stability in the top division.

Shortly after its cup victory, FK Dostyk withdrew from the league and ceased operations in 1993–1994. Financial and organizational difficulties led to its rapid disappearance from professional football. Although short-lived, the club is remembered for its brief but successful existence and its unexpected national cup triumph during the early years of independent Kazakh football.

name: FC Akzhayik
content:
FC Akzhayik is a professional football club based in Oral (Uralsk), Kazakhstan. Founded in 1968, the club has been a long-standing part of Kazakh football and is one of the traditional teams from the western region of the country. It plays its home matches at the Petr Atoyan Stadium and has participated in both the Kazakhstan Premier League and the First Division throughout its history.

The club has undergone many name changes over the decades, including Uralets, Uralets-Arma, Zhangir, Naryn, Batys, and finally Akzhayik in 2004. These changes reflected different sponsorships and administrative reforms during the Soviet and post-Soviet periods. Like many regional clubs, Akzhayik often moved between divisions, experiencing both promotions to the top flight and relegations to lower tiers.

Akzhayik’s main achievement is winning the Kazakhstan First Division title in 2015, which secured promotion to the Premier League. While the club has not won major top-flight trophies, it has had competitive seasons and produced steady performances in domestic competitions. Over the years, FC Akzhayik has remained an important representative of football in western Kazakhstan, known for its resilience despite financial and sporting challenges.
